run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:47:57Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real failure evidence: frontend-proxy's 'ingress' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR with http.status_code 504 and ~15s duration, and its Envoy access log shows 'POST /api/checkout' returning '504 UT response_timeout' after 15000 ms against upstream 'frontend'. In traces, the /api/checkout request exceeds the proxy's 15s limit (frontend POST /api/checkout 15.44s) because checkout's Kafka produce span 'orders publish' takes 15.24s while every other checkout child (payment, email, cart, currency, product-catalog) answers in milliseconds. Checkout's own container log shows Kafka writes of ~130-500 microseconds until 00:45:30 and then 11.4-16.7 s per write from 00:55, together with 'connection refused' to kafka:9092 and 'circuit breaker is open' between 00:46:22 and 00:47:08, exactly when Deployment kafka was rolled (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:45:26Z, identical container template/image) and its broker came back with a freshly created empty orders-0 partition (high watermark 0) on the ephemeral /tmp/kafka-logs. The only switched-on fault-injection setting found is 'kafkaQueueProblems' = on (100) in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, whose description matches the observed queue problem, and flagd was itself rolled at 00:14:07Z with an unchanged pod template, which is the only mechanism seen for applying that file. Conclusion is partial: the declared overload/consumer-lag fault was not directly measured, the time the flag value was changed is unknown (change history is not integrated), and what issued the two rollout restarts is unknown; the counter-evidence is that Kafka writes were sub-millisecond at 00:44:30-00:45:30 while flagd (loaded with the same file) had already been running since 00:14:07.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's Envoy access log records 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout' with a 15000 ms upstream time to 'frontend' (e.g. 00:54:27.592Z, 00:54:31.839Z, 00:54:45.237Z); the log had 106 such 504 lines in the 00:50-00:55 slice read.

Trace 8ebb654aa5b3473caa81840f4b2113d6 (00:56:20Z) shows frontend-proxy span operation 'ingress' 15.001s with status tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR, parented by the load-generator POST span; its child 'router frontend egress' ran 15.001s, while frontend 'POST /api/checkout' ran 15.444s and checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' ran 15.440s with child 'orders publish' at 15.238s; payment charge was 1.487ms, email send_order_confirmation 72ms and cart EmptyCart 115ms in the same trace.

An earlier failing trace 79c5bb8a4370c04eb3b81c574cf08d2c (00:47:05Z) shows the same shape: frontend-proxy 'ingress' 15.001s http.status_code=504 with child 'router frontend egress' http.status_code=0, frontend POST /api/checkout 16.003s, checkout PlaceOrder 16.000s and checkout 'orders publish' 15.771s while cart/currency/product-catalog/shipping/quote/email/payment children completed in milliseconds.

The checkout container logged Kafka writes with microsecond durations before the Kafka rollout: 'Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration: 174.841µs ... 532.547µs' for lines timestamped 00:44:30.207Z through 00:45:30.311Z.

The checkout container logged the same message with second-scale durations after the Kafka rollout: 'Successful to write message ... duration: 16.66880895s' at 00:55:02.041Z, 14.37101277s at 00:55:02.112Z, 13.104790752s at 00:55:04.445Z, 12.598711622s at 00:55:06.072Z and 11.452121497s at 00:55:07.529Z.

Checkout container logs between 00:46:22.964Z and 00:47:08.704Z contain 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused', 'Failed to write message: kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to' and 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open'; the client re-registered at 00:47:11.742Z ('Connected to broker at kafka:9092 (registered as #1)').

Deployment otel-demo/kafka was rolled at 00:45:26Z: new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 was created 00:45:26Z with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:45:26Z while the previous ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 (created 00:12:21Z) carries no such annotation; Deployment events show ScalingReplicaSet 00:45:26Z (0 to 1) and 00:45:28Z (1 to 0) plus ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate 00:45:26Z and SuccessfulDelete 00:45:28Z, pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 Started 00:45:27Z and pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 'Stopping container kafka' 00:45:28Z.

The two kafka ReplicaSets kafka-5c9d7cc485 and kafka-ff7884766 have identical container specs (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka, same env including KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092, same ports and resources); the only template difference seen is the restartedAt annotation, so this was a configuration-only restart.

The Kafka broker pod log of kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 shows '[Kafka Server started]' at 00:47:03.030Z, controller replies 'CreateTopics ... CreatableTopic(name=\'orders\', numPartitions=1, replicationFactor=1 ...): TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS' at 00:47:07.12Z, and then '[Broker id=1] Creating new partition orders-0', 'Created log for partition orders-0 in /tmp/kafka-logs/orders-0' and 'Log loaded for partition orders-0 with initial high watermark 0' (leader epoch 0) at 00:47:07.8Z; consumer groups fraud-detection and accounting were rebalanced at 00:47:08.17Z and 00:47:10.03Z.
Deployment otel-demo/kafka declares no volumes and no volumeMounts on its container, so the broker's log directory /tmp/kafka-logs is not persisted.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) defines flag 'kafkaQueueProblems' with state ENABLED, description 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike', variants {off: 0, on: 100} and defaultVariant 'on'; every other flag in the same file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'.

Deployment otel-demo/flagd, the pod that serves this flag file, was itself rolled at 00:14:07Z: ReplicaSet flagd-f546d44c9 was created 00:14:07Z with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:14:07Z, while the previous ReplicaSet flagd-c47676d99 (00:12:21Z) has no such annotation and now has 0 replicas; the pod's init container copies the flagd-config ConfigMap file into the emptyDir read by flagd.

In traces_span_metrics_calls_total, the only frontend-proxy span with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR is span_name 'ingress' (frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' errors are 0), and its 10-minute increase rose from ~5.3 at 00:34:00Z to ~12.6 at 00:46:00Z and then 28.4 at 00:47:00Z, 65.3 at 00:49:00Z, 138.9 at 00:53:00Z and 171.7 at 01:00:00Z.

frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans longer than 5s and longer than 10s were 0 from 00:29:00Z through 00:46:00Z and first appear at 00:47:00Z (24.4 spans >5s per 5m, 13.3 spans >10s per 5m), rising to 136.7 per 5m >5s at 00:50:00Z and 120.7 per 5m >10s at 01:00:00Z.

Among frontend spans, only the checkout path exceeds 5s: 'POST /api/checkout' (and its 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' children, plus 'POST') counted 0 over 5s at 00:22:57Z-00:42:57Z, then 47.4 per 10m at 00:47:57Z, 188.6 at 00:52:57Z and 296.1 at 00:57:57Z, while GET /, GET /api/data, GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, grpc CartService/GetCart and grpc ProductCatalogService/GetProduct remained 0.
Checkout error spans are exclusively span_name 'orders publish': 19.18 per 10m at 00:47:57Z, 15.40 per 10m at 00:52:57Z and 0 at 00:57:57Z; no other checkout span_name returned error counts.

Spans longer than 5s at 00:57:57Z existed only for checkout (588.1 per 10m), frontend (1175.1), frontend-proxy (592.3), accounting (17.7) and recommendation (1.04); cart, currency, email, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote and shipping each returned 0, and ad returned 0 at that point.

Error-span increases by service over the window are: frontend-proxy 185.6 per 10m at 00:57:57Z, checkout 19.2 then 15.4 then 0, ad ~1.05 per 10m from 00:42:57Z, recommendation ~1.05 per 10m, and 0 for accounting, fraud-detection, frontend and payment; cart, currency, email, product-catalog, quote and shipping were not returned for that query.

Accounting span 'order-consumed' spent time above 5s throughout the sampled window: 5.2 per 10m at 00:22:57Z rising to 17.7 per 10m at 00:57:57Z, while the same span's total call volume stayed around 384-415 per 10m before 00:47Z and 298-312 per 10m after 00:52Z (it did not rise).

Pod inventory in otel-demo at query time: frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295, frontend-675fd7b5c5-tsdtv and checkout-5dccddf8bb-6qppz are Running/ready with restartCount 0; kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 started 00:45:26Z with restartCount 0 and is ready; fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm is Running/ready with restartCount 2 and lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137.
A Warning event at 00:38:32Z records 'Back-off restarting failed container fraud-detection in pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm_otel-demo'.

frontend-proxy access-log lines between 00:24:00Z and the 4 MiB read cut at 00:44:01.5Z contain no '504' status entry; the two lines matching ' 504 ' were 200 and 308 responses whose millisecond durations were 504 and 505.

The frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans present before the burst were short: over 00:34:00Z-00:44:00Z the error-span increase totalled 11.58 per 10m and the cumulative bucket le=1000.0 also equalled 11.58, i.e. every one of them finished within 1s (none reached the 5000/10000/15000 buckets).

Non-checkout frontend-proxy requests were still succeeding during the incident: the access log shows e.g. 'GET /api/products/... 200 - via_upstream', 'POST /api/cart ... 200 - via_upstream' and 'GET /api/data?contextKeys=... 200 - via_upstream' at 00:55:06-00:55:08Z.

Kafka produce latency cannot be attributed to the switched-on flag alone: with flagd (serving the current file that has kafkaQueueProblems=on) already running since its 00:14:07Z rollout, checkout wrote to Kafka in 130-533 microseconds between 00:44:30Z and 00:45:30Z, i.e. the step to 11-17s began only with the kafka Deployment rollout at 00:45:26Z.

Most likely origin: the fault-injection setting 'kafkaQueueProblems' = on (100) held in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, applied to the running flagd by that Deployment's 00:14:07Z rollout, is the declared Kafka queue fault; its mechanism/consequences are the broker rollout at 00:45:26Z, the empty recreated orders-0 partition, checkout Kafka writes of 11-17s and 'circuit breaker is open' failures, checkout PlaceOrder ~15.4s exceeding Envoy's 15000 ms response_timeout on POST /api/checkout, and the resulting frontend-proxy 504 error spans that fire RequestErrorRate.

Alternative candidate that remains: the 00:45:26Z configuration-only rollout of Deployment kafka alone degraded the produce path, because it replaced the broker with an empty ephemeral /tmp/kafka-logs (orders-0 recreated with high watermark 0) and the write-duration step change coincides exactly with that restart, independent of the flag; this alternative is not rejected because the flag value's change time is unknown.

A slow downstream of checkout other than Kafka does not explain the 15s stall: in the failing traces every other checkout child was fast (payment Charge 1.487ms, email POST /send_order_confirmation 72ms, cart EmptyCart 115ms, product-catalog 86-479µs, currency Convert 0.4-54ms), and cart, currency, email, payment, product-catalog, quote and shipping each had 0 spans over 5s at 00:57:57Z while checkout had 588.1 per 10m.

frontend-proxy being broken or restarting is not the cause: its pod has restartCount 0 and is ready, its access log explicitly labels the failures '504 UT response_timeout' against upstream 'frontend' at 15000 ms, and other routes through the same proxy returned 200 via_upstream during the incident.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so I cannot tell when ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config's kafkaQueueProblems value was changed to 'on', nor who or what issued the flagd 00:14:07Z and kafka 00:45:26Z rollout restarts (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotations).

The declared fault itself was not directly observed: no Kafka lag, topic-size, produce/consume latency or broker request metrics exist in the target (a metric-name query for .*kafka.*|.*flagd.*|.*queue.* returned nothing), accounting 'order-consumed' call volume did not rise (384-415 per 10m before 00:47Z, 298-312 per 10m at/after 00:52Z), and queue overload / consumer-side lag are inferred only from span durations and application log durations.

The ~5-12 frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans per 10 minutes seen in the metrics before 00:44Z (all finishing within 1s) are unexplained: the frontend-proxy access log slice read for 00:24:00Z-00:44:01.5Z contained no 504 status line, and Jaeger retained no traces from that period (traces_search_by_tags for frontend-proxy error spans in 00:28-00:30Z and 00:45-00:46Z returned nothing).

Queries that returned no data and therefore support no negative conclusion here: list_prometheus_rules for RequestErrorRate returned no rules (tool has no time range), and the two metric-range queries for the >14000ms and >15000ms ingress buckets returned no series.
The previous Kafka broker instance's logs are unavailable (pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 was deleted at 00:45:28Z), so the broker-side state before the restart cannot be read.

Container log streams for frontend-proxy and checkout were readable only through ~00:55:07Z, so the 00:56-01:00Z behaviour rests on metrics and traces alone; the frontend-proxy log read for 00:24-00:46Z also hit the 4 MiB read limit at 00:44:01.5Z.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zcxzm restarted twice with last termination OOMKilled (exit 137) and got a BackOff event at 00:38:32Z; no OOM event or memory-limit evidence was read, its log filter for err/error/fail/panic/memory returned nothing, and no fraud-detection error span or fraud span in the checkout traces ties it to this 504 cause, so it stays an unresolved separate finding.
next_steps: Ask the change-management/audit owner for the history of ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (kafkaQueueProblems) and for whoever issued the flagd rollout at 00:14:07Z and the kafka rollout at 00:45:26Z.

Add Kafka broker and consumer-group lag metrics (or scrape the broker JMX) to measure the declared kafkaQueueProblems effect directly, and compare produce latency for orders before/after the flag value changes.

Confirm the frontend/Envoy route timeout configuration that turns ~15s checkout latency into 504s, and consider whether checkout's Kafka produce path should use a bounded timeout shorter than the proxy timeout.
Investigate fraud-detection's OOMKilled restarts and its memory limit separately, and check whether checkout calls fraud-detection on this order path.
